headlines.title: Woman ‘going after vehicles with a knife' causes traffic backup on Hwy. 101 in San Jose
headlines.description: A woman allegedly “going after vehicles with a knife” caused major traffic delays on Highway 101 in San Jose on Saturday morning, according to the California Highway Patrol. CHP said it received a call around 11:10 a.m. regarding a woman walking near Highway 101, just south of Bernal Road. Authorities said the initial report indicated she was walking from the right-hand shoulder toward the center divide and was later reported on the southbound side, walking northbound in the southbound lanes. At 11:13 a.m., CHP said the woman was reportedly “going after vehicles with a knife.” Images of the scene show a severe backup caused by the incident. Drivers can also be observed exiting their vehicles. CHP said lanes 1 and 2 were open on southbound 101, just south of Highway 85, at 11:43 a.m. CHP has not released any information about what happened to the woman.

headlines.title: San Francisco police investigate homicide in Bayview District
headlines.description: The San Francisco Police Department is investigating a homicide in the Bayview District after they found a man suffering from a gunshot wound, police announced Saturday. According to the police, they responded to the 1100 block of Wisconsin Street regarding a shooting on Friday, at around 8:38 p.m. When they arrived, officers found a man suffering from an apparent gunshot wound. However, despite first aid and lifesaving efforts by paramedics, the victim succumbed to his wound and was pronounced deceased on scene, police said. Anyone with information is asked to call the SFPD 415-575-4444 or text a tip to TIP411 and begin the message with SFPD. You may remain anonymous.

headlines.title: Rep. DeSaulnier's Walnut Creek district office receives ‘suspicious envelope'
headlines.description: Congressman Mark DeSaulnier said a “suspicious envelope” was delivered to his Walnut Creek district office Friday afternoon. According to DeSaulnier, the U.S. Capitol Police reported that several congressional district offices have received “suspicious envelopes” containing “threatening letters and a white powdery substance.” He said the envelope delivered to his district office matched that description. The Contra Costa County Sheriff’s Office said there was a “large presence” near DeSaulnier’s office. Here’s DeSaulnier’s full statement: “Following reports from U.S. Capitol Police of identical suspicious envelopes containing threatening letters and a white powdery substance that were delivered to other Congressional district offices across the nation, a member of our team identified a letter matching the description and return address, immediately secured the envelope without opening it, and called local law enforcement and U.S. Capitol Police. “Threats and political violence seem to have reached a fever pitch in our country, and I urge my fellow Americans to stand united against such attempts at undermining our democracy. “My priority remains the safety and security of my team, and I am thankful for the quick and decisive response. We remain committed to serving CA-10 residents and will not be deterred from this important work by threats.” The listed return address was a Manhattan location linked to the Democratic Socialists of America, but the group said they have not had offices there in years. Minority leader Chuck Schumer had a threatening letter intercepted, according to a spokesman. California Senator Alex Padilla says he was also alerted that his office was targeted. Local offices of several other elected leaders also received these letters. Representative Zoe Lofgren posted that law enforcement was immediately called after her San Jose office received a suspicious letter, adding that her staffers are safe and the investigation is ongoing. Representative Jimmy Panetta says staff opened an envelope Friday morning and realized there was powder inside. She immediately put the envelopes in the garbage can and cleared staff members out of the office and called 911. Law enforcement officials said initial testing of the envelope was negative. But experts say Capitol Hill police, the FBI and postal inspectors have to treat these letter threats seriously. “The impact could be deadly, because the one time that you’re wrong, you know innocent bystanders could end up, could end up deceased or very sick,” Former NJ FBI Director Timothy Gallagher said. These letters have now been sent nationwide, with some being delivered to state officers in Louisiana, Ohio and Oklahoma on Thursday. The mailings come three weeks before election day, and an investigation to track the sender could take some time.

headlines.title: Valkyries fans prepare for the team's historic debut in the WNBA Finals
headlines.description: Fans of the Golden State Valkyries are gearing up for a milestone event in Bay Area sports history: the Valkyries’ debut in the WNBA Finals. The team, which is only in its second year have garnered enormous support from fans for their culture on and off the court. Game one of their series against the Atlanta Dream will start at 12:30 p.m. Pacific in San Francisco at Chase Center. It is possible the series could run up to seven games depending on how long it takes a team to win four games. Even before the game started, fans have been proudly wearing their Valkyries gear around the Bay Area and planning out how they’ll watch the games. At Rikki’s, a sports bar in San Francisco’s Castro that prioritizes women’s sports, staff are preparing for what they will expect to be days of lines out the door when the finals are on. So far, the bar has been at capacity during the Valkyries post-season run, as fans look for chances to cheer on the team together. “This moment is something I think I hoped for but did not think would happen this fast, for this team to be this good and this kind of connected to the community,” said Danielle Thoe, a co-owner and general manager at Rikki’s. Thoe said the Valkyries have been very supportive of sports bars in their network, sending along freebies and team merch to watch parties. “I think the Valkyries are showing that like womens sports fandom has no limit,” Thoe said, adding that the Valkyries success comes at a time when momentum around women’s sports in the Bay Area is on the rise. The Valkyries have hit many milestones during their only two ears of existence. The team sold out every single home game they have played so far. Last year, they became the first WNBA expansion team to advance to the playoffs in their inaugural year. The team has also built a vibrant fanbase and now have a real shot at being league champions. “I cannot explain how much excitement I have inside and among everyone I know, the number of texts I am getting,” said Julie Dorf of Berkeley, a season ticket holder. “This is just one more really neat thing for the Bay Area, for the city, for California,” said Tracey McNamara of Mendocino County, who is in San Francisco to attend game one of the finals on Saturday. The Valkyries plan to have activities for fans outside Thrive City on game days. Sports bars across the Bay Area are planning watch parties for the finals as well.

headlines.title: Power restored to some Bay Area customers affected by PG&E shutoffs
headlines.description: A PG&E spokesperson said Friday afternoon that power has been restored to some, but not yet all, of the customers affected across five Bay Area counties by power shutoffs the utility company implemented starting Wednesday to prevent its equipment from sparking wildfires. PG&E had announced what it calls Public Safety Power Shutoffs for about 90,000 customers across 29 counties starting Wednesday evening due to dry and windy weather. The National Weather Service issued a Red Flag Warning for interior North Bay mountains that was in effect through 11 a.m. Friday because of elevated wildfire dangers due to low humidity and wind gusts of up to 60 mph at the highest peaks. Thousands of the affected customers were in five Bay Area counties — Alameda, Contra Costa, Napa, Solano and Sonoma. PG&E spokesperson Tamar Sarkissian said Alameda County had 4,720 customers affected, and 1,666 of those had power restored as of Friday afternoon. Contra Costa County had 1,607 customers and 458 of those restored, while Napa County had 2,915 customers affected and 323 restored so far. In Solano County, only 32 customers were affected and all of those have their power back on, while in Sonoma County, crews had restored power to 952 of the 2,0444 customers affected, according to Sarkissian. The power shutoffs are expected to last into Saturday, though milder weather is expected this weekend and into early next week. People can visit pge.com/pspsupdates to find out if their location is affected by the power shutoffs. PG&E has opened community resource centers in affected areas that offer restrooms, device charging, Wi-Fi, bottled water and snacks, and other supplies. A list of the centers by county can be found online. PG&E is also encouraging customers who may need additional support to contact 211, including those who rely on power for medical needs or who have a disability.

headlines.title: Valkyries fever ramps up in Bay Area ahead of WNBA Finals Game 1 at Ballhalla
headlines.description: Bay Area hoops will be in the national spotlight with the WNBA Finals tipping off Saturday at San Francisco’s Chase Center. The best-of-seven series features the Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream both competing for each respective franchise’s first title. Both teams are known for being defensive juggernauts. Golden State’s deep playoff run has united the Bay Area, with fans attending Chase Center games expected to make “Ballhalla” a nightmare for the Dream. What were the results from Valkyries vs. Dream regular season games? The Valkyries swept the regular-season series against the Dream, winning two games at home and one on the road. Golden State recorded victories of 77-66 and 78-75 over Atlanta at Ballhalla in late June before beating the Dream 88-83 in the most recent meeting July 4. Golden State Valkyries Oct 15 WNBA Oct 12 WNBA Oct 12 Postseason experience Atlanta is looking for its first title, but have made three Finals trips ahead of this year’s series against Golden State. The Valkyries made history in their inaugural season last year by qualifying for the 2025 WNBA Playoffs as the No. 8 seed with a 23–21 regular-season. Who has home-court advantage in the WNBA Finals? The Valkyries have home court due to being the higher seed. Golden State will host Games 1 and 2 at Ballhalla, along with the potential Games 5 and 7. How to watch Valkyries vs. Dream in the WNBA Finals The series will air across NBC and USA Network. Games 1 and 4 will be on NBC Bay Area. All games can also be streamed on Peacock. Where to stream Valkyries vs. Dream WNBA Finals games live online In addition to Peacock, there are other platforms where the Finals can be streamed. NBC broadcasts can also be seen on NBC.com and the NBC app, while USA Network broadcasts are available to watch on USANetwork.com and the USA Network app. Valkyries vs. Dream WNBA Finals schedule Here’s the full Finals broadcast schedule: Game 1: Dream at Valkyries — Saturday, Oct. 17, 3:30 p.m. ET/12:30 p.m. PT, NBC and Peacock Game 2: Dream at Valkyries — Monday, Oct. 19, 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT, Peacock and USA Network Game 3: Valkyries at Dream — Wednesday, Oct. 21, 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT, Peacock and USA Network Game 4: Valkyries at Dream — Saturday, Oct. 24, 1 p.m. ET/10 a.m. PT, NBC and Peacock Game 5 (if necessary): Dream at Valkyries — Monday, Oct. 26, 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT, Peacock and USA Network Game 6 (if necessary): Valkyries at Dream — Thursday, Oct. 29, 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT, Peacock and USA Network Game 7 (if necessary): Dream at Valkyries — Saturday, Oct. 31, 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT, Peacock and USA Network

headlines.title: Zombie shooter game based on San Francisco's Tenderloin causes controversy
headlines.description: The creator of a controversial zombie shooting game set in San Francisco’s Tenderloin neighborhood has taken the game down following city leaders’ requests. The game, called “Tenderloin Night Shift,” invited players to indiscriminately shoot zombies in a neighborhood that resembles the actual area. The game includes signature images of the city, including Waymos and e-scooters. In the game, players were invited to “meet the locals” as the screen shows a person folded over, much like someone struggling with a fentanyl addiction. Mayor Daniel Lurie called it horrific. “There’s no accounting for taste or people’s terrible ideas. This is a bad one and we reject it. It doesn’t speak for San Francisco values,” Lurie said. Lurie has been touting the city’s noticeable recovery from pandemic issues, including open-air drug markets and a boom in homeless encampments, over the last two years. NBC Bay Area reached out to the creator of the video game for comment in an interview either on camera or by phone, but he declined. In his initial response, the creator said he based the video game on what he sees in the Tenderloin on his commute to and from work every day. Pierre-Louis Biojout, the founder of a startup called NanoCorp, says he rejects the suggestion that the game promotes violence against residents. He wrote in part, “It was not intended to depict shooting real people or to target a particular demographic or group.” Over the last few days, people have taken to social media to blast the game and his attempts to advertise it. Advocates for the unhoused and for people experiencing drug addiction have said he’s monetizing people’s suffering. Supervisor Bilal Mahmoud, who represents the Tenderloin, says Biojout’s video game comes from a pretentious and privileged point of view. “I would say that he represents a minority voice. On the very same day this started to blow up, I was working with other people in the entrepreneurial community to announce the investment in the Arts District to support arts and independent theater and revitalizing the Tenderloin corridor on Market,” he said. Biojout recently said he’s taken the game offline and its promotional materials. He says he’s also refunded al money to advertisers and made a personal donation to a local foundation that services the unhoused and people in addiction recovery.

headlines.title: Santa Clara University to offer free education to eligible low-income students
headlines.description: For millions of low-income families, sending a student to a private university is next to impossible. Santa Clara University says it has a plan to change that. Beginning next fall, any California applicant who is accepted into the South Bay university and whose family earns less than $150,000 a year will receive a free college education as part of the university’s recently expanded California Promise program. “As a Jesuit institution, the university has made a commitment to try to meet 100% of demonstrated need of students,” said Cindy Tirado, the university’s director of financial aid. In addition to qualifying for admittance, eligible families also have to possess assets worth less than $120,000. Final eligibility will be determined using the applicant’s Federal Student Aid application, known as FAFSA. “I think a lot of times people think private college isn’t unattainable,” Tirado said. “This would make it attainable for a lot of families that don’t see us as a possibility. It’s going to be able to get them access to an education that they never thought they could have.”

headlines.title: Black Panther Party legacy and history to be honored in Oakland
headlines.description: Former members of the Black Panther Party are reuniting with a new generation this weekend to honor the party’s history and legacy after being founded in Oakland six decades ago. A revolution started in Oakland 60 years ago, when Huey P. Newton and Bobby Seale founded the Black Panther Party amid police brutality and racial inequality. Beyond the black berets and images of armed resistance was a movement building programs to help people survive. “This legacy was a legacy of love. It was based on the love of our community that young men and women laid their lives on the line to fight for the rights of, not only Black people, but all oppressed people,” co-founder of Black Panther Party Museum and Dr. Huey P. Newton Foundation Fredrika Newton said. That led to 65 survival programs, from free meals for children to healthcare and community support, all meant to fill gaps the groups’ leaders say the government wasn’t meeting. This weekend, Panther veterans from across the world will meet in Oakland for four days of workshops, cultural programs, and celebrations. It’s a surreal moment for Fredrika Newton. “It feels other worldly in many ways. It’s beautiful to see party members coming from all over the country. For many, it’s the first time that many have been under the same roof since the 60s,” she said. Black Panthers from around the nation say the legacy lives on. “We are about the connecting from the old to the young. So, this is very important that they see us, knowing that they have passed the watch to a generation that is still dedicated, that is still in the struggle and will not give up,” Yusef Miller with the San Diego Black Panther Chapter said. Around 1,000 high school and college students are attending the weekend celebration for free, passing the history to the next generation. “We need to keep the Black Panther party alive. It’s bringing an awareness to Oakland that maybe some of the younger students and younger people know about how important the Black Party is,” Metwest High School community school manager Carinne Salnave said. Four blocks of Broadway are being renamed Black Panther Party Boulevard on Saturday. Mayor Barbara Lee, who worked with the party as a community worker, says its impact continues to shape the fight for justice today. “No one can deny that the Black Panther Party contributed to our freedom and to racial and economic justice,” she said. “They were the north star,” she said.

headlines.title: San Francisco's Ripley's Believe It or Not! to close in December
headlines.description: Ripley’s Believe It or Not! will close its Fisherman’s Wharf location in San Francisco on Dec. 1 after 60 years. The attraction opened on Feb. 2, 1967. Notable visitors included Michael Jackson, Joe DiMaggio and former San Francisco Mayor Willie Brown. “We’ve had nearly 60 unbelievable years at Fisherman’s Wharf, and we want these final weeks to be a celebration,” said Jim Pattison Jr., president of Ripley’s Believe It or Not! World Entertainment. “Whether you visited us as a kid, brought your own kids years later, or have somehow never made it through our doors, we hope you’ll come see us one more time.” To mark the end of its run, every Thursday leading up to the final day guests can experience Ripley’s Believe It or Not! for $19.67. Admission on closing day will return to original 1967 attraction prices at just $1.50 for adults and 75 cents for kids. Some of its strangest treasures are also going up for auction. Guests can bid on items such as Joe DiMaggio’s crutches, a chicken-wire portrait of Janis Joplin and toothpick replicas of the Golden Gate Bridge.

headlines.title: Man injured in shooting after vehicle collision in Menlo Park
headlines.description: A shooting in Menlo Park on Thursday night injured a 47-year-old man who had three children in his vehicle and had just gotten into a collision with the suspected shooter’s car, according to police. Menlo Park police responded at 8:39 p.m. to reports of gunfire in the area of Bay and Hedge roads, located near Flood Park. Officers arrived and found the man with a gunshot wound and three children between the ages of 8 and 14 in his car. None of the children were hurt and the man was taken to a hospital and is expected to survive, police said. Investigators learned that a non-injury collision had occurred and when the man exited his vehicle to exchange information, someone in the other vehicle shot him. The vehicle was only described as a “small white car” and police did not share any details about the suspected shooter. Anyone with information about the case is asked to contact Detective Marcial Barron-Villa at mbarron-villa@menlopark.gov or 650-847-7438.

headlines.title: Mail-in ballots stolen from Daly City post office
headlines.description: The U.S. Postal Service is investigating after vote-by-mail ballots for San Mateo County were stolen from a Daly City post office, the county’s Registration & Elections Division said Thursday. The Elections Division said it was notified Wednesday of the mail theft that reportedly included mail-in ballots. The number of ballots that were stolen is still unknown. The county is working with USPS to investigate. Voters who are concerned that their ballots may have been affected by the theft may request a replacement ballot online or in person at any vote center in the county. Online requests for a replacement ballot must be submitted by Oct. 27 to allow sufficient time for mailing. Voters are encouraged to look up the status of their mail-in ballots through the California Secretary of State’s free ballot tracking service, “Where’s My Ballot.” The platform notifies voters when their ballot is mailed, received, and processed by the county elections division. There are currently three vote centers open in the county. Additional centers will open on Saturday, Oct. 24 and Saturday, Oct. 31, bringing the total to 50 vote centers. For a list of vote centers and ballot drop off locations, go to smcacre.gov. Voters with questions about their ballot status can contact the elections division at registrar@smcacre.gov or 650-312-5222.
